independent_s3_readback.implementation: Python urllib + hashlib/hmac, no proxy or local spool reads

verified_behaviors: Every download uses the original submission credential and current Computer connect/read plus original Workspace read grants, checked before and after object IO.

Synthetic PostgreSQL/HTTP contracts reject cross-credential and cross-organization reads before IO, pending publication, altered/short/oversized/missing/rejected object bytes, and seven forms of authority loss during a successful or failed GET. No database lock spans remote IO.

Binary, empty and truncated retained streams preserve original bytes. Closed connections and removed modify grants do not revoke retained output when read authority remains; removing Workspace read does.

HTTP tests cover explicit optional configuration, capabilities, authenticated errors, fixed stdout/stderr selectors, Origin rejection, unsupported ranges/queries, and four slots retained by unconsumed bodies.

Fresh service processes read sixteen streams from eight real S3 publications, including command failure, timeout, truncation and publication recovery. All bytes and hashes match original gVisor reports and independent signed Python S3 GETs.
Reads do not create new dispatches, startup grants, execution completions or writer drains. Unknown stays Unknown after output recovery/download.
experiment_notes: No registered repo-sandbox target was available. Reused the authorized disposable QEMU workflow: 4 vCPU, 6 GiB RAM, 24 GiB overlay.

The first real HTTP check found chunked transfer framing from the response-body wrapper. Downloads now set their verified Content-Length explicitly; the complete sixteen-case rerun passed with no transfer encoding.
The first attempt left one earlier test execution outside final-run counts. Independent collection restricts database and object assertions to the final test organization.
The previously verified supervisor OCI archive was reused because its packaged supervisor SHA-256 exactly matches the current Bazel binary; there are no supervisor/runtime changes in this increment.
limits: Single-node Linux/K3s/gVisor/JuiceFS/S3 component verification; isolated HTTP object transport, not production TLS or HA certification.
Four gateway slots cover fetch/authorization and body ownership until HTTP transport consumes or drops the body; this is not a deployment-wide connection or bandwidth limit.
No live tailing, ranges, output sharing across credentials, automatic dispatch, browser/ComputerView, cross-node fencing or full product acceptance.
